items.title: Expense Tracker: Add recurring expense templates
items.body:
## Context
Repeated entries such as software subscriptions must currently be entered manually. Recurring templates would demonstrate another business workflow without requiring background services.

## Scope and acceptance criteria
- Support monthly templates with description, fixed category, USD amount, start date, and optional end date.
- On opening the app, preview due entries and let the user confirm which to add. Do not silently invent actual spending.
- Define and document short-month behavior, including templates dated on the 29th through 31st.
- Persist occurrence identifiers so reloads and repeated confirmations cannot duplicate an occurrence.
- Let users pause, edit, and delete templates without rewriting previously confirmed expenses.
- Add checks for missed months, leap years, duplicate prevention, cancellation, and failed saves.

Keep processing local and explicit; no scheduled server jobs, bank integrations, or daily/weekly recurrence in this first iteration.

items.title: Expense Tracker: Support user-defined expense categories
items.body:
## Context
The initial sample uses five fixed categories: Supplies, Travel, Meals, Software, and Other. Custom categories are a follow-up enhancement for different small-business use cases.

## Scope and acceptance criteria
- Provide an accessible workflow to add and rename categories with trimmed, bounded names and case-insensitive duplicate detection.
- Use stable category identifiers so renaming does not orphan saved expenses or change their financial totals.
- Migrate existing version-1 expenses without data loss and update the form, filters, summaries, and CSV consistently.
- Require explicit reassignment before deleting a category used by an expense.
- Keep unknown/corrupt saved data protected, with an actionable error rather than silently dropping entries.
- Add migration, rename, reassignment, duplicate-name, reload, and storage-failure checks.

Do not add nested categories or a backend.

items.title: [Server Submission]: Expense Tracker (mcp-expense-tracker)
items.body:
### GitHub Repository URL

https://github.com/theluckystrike/mcp-servers/tree/main/servers/expense-tracker

### Logo Image

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/theluckystrike/mcp-servers/main/assets/expense-tracker-logo.png

(400x400 PNG, committed in the repository at `assets/expense-tracker-logo.png`.)

### Installation Testing

- [ ] I have tested that Cline can successfully set up this server using only the README.md and/or llms-install.md file
- [X] The server is stable and ready for public use

### Additional Information

**Why this is useful for Cline users:** Logs a business expense from one chat line, splits the gross receipt amount into net and VAT with `vat_rate`, categorises new expenses from stored merchant rules, attaches a receipt by path and sha256 for an audit trail, and prices a mileage trip from a built-in regional rate table (PL, UK, US, EU). Summaries group by category, project, month or merchant, always per currency and never mixed. `expense_to_invoice` hands the unbilled billable expenses of a project straight to `mcp-invoice` as ready line items, so a Cline user already tracking work and invoicing in chat gets expense rebilling in the same loop.

**Install path.** The repository is a monorepo; this submission is the `servers/expense-tracker` subfolder. It ships `servers/expense-tracker/llms-install.md` with the exact steps an agent should follow: prerequisites, the run command, merge-ready config JSON for Cline (`cline_mcp_settings.json`), Claude Desktop, Claude Code and Cursor, a verification call (`license_status`), and alternatives (.mcpb bundle, from source, Docker).

**Honest note on the first checkbox.** The npm package `@theluckystrike/mcp-expense-tracker` is not published yet, so the `npx -y @theluckystrike/mcp-expense-tracker` line does not resolve today. `llms-install.md` says so at the top and directs the agent to the from-source path (`git clone`, `npm install`, `npm run build`, then `node <abs path>/servers/expense-tracker/dist/index.js`), which is verified working. I have followed those steps by hand end to end (build, then an `initialize` and `tools/list` JSON-RPC round trip over stdio) but I have not run the install through Cline itself, so I am leaving that box unchecked rather than claiming it. The npx path will be correct as soon as the package is published, with no change to the config shown.

**Technical facts.** MIT licensed. TypeScript on `@modelcontextprotocol/sdk` ^1.30.0, stdio transport, Node >= 18, pure JavaScript with no native dependencies. All data is stored in plain JSON files under `${XDG_DATA_HOME:-~/.local/share}/mcp-servers/expense-tracker/`; no telemetry, no account, no API key, no network access at all. An optional offline-verified license key lifts free-tier limits (30-day list/summary history, capped projects, category rules and export rows); every tool works without it. Security contact: support@zovo.one.

items.title: Improve Expense Tracker Dashboard UI/UX
items.body:
**Description**
Improve the Expense Tracker dashboard to make it more user-friendly, responsive, visually consistent, and easier to navigate on laptop screens.

**Problems to Address**

**1. Reduce Empty Space**
The dashboard content is concentrated in the center, leaving excessive empty space on both sides.
Increase the maximum content width and use available screen space efficiently.
Align summary cards, transaction tables, and charts consistently.
Maintain responsive layouts for different screen sizes.
**2. Improve the Transaction Table**
Add a search field to find transactions by title.
Add date and category filters.
Support sorting by date, amount, and transaction type.
Format currency amounts using Indian numbering conventions (e.g., ₹10,000 instead of 10000).
Keep Edit and Delete actions accessible and consistent.
**3. Improve Chart Visibility and Readability**
Prevent charts from being cut off or extending beyond the visible content area.
Give every chart a descriptive title.
Add appropriate labels, legends, and tooltips.
Use consistent chart dimensions and responsive sizing.
Ensure chart data and labels remain readable on laptop screens.
**4. Establish a Consistent Design System**
Replace the inconsistent navigation colors with a cohesive color palette.
Standardize button styles, border radii, typography, and spacing.
Use consistent colors for income, expenses, and balance.
Improve visual hierarchy so important financial information stands out.
Maintain sufficient contrast and clear interactive states.
**Expected Outcome**
The dashboard should use available laptop screen space effectively, make transaction management easier, display charts clearly, and provide a consistent, professional user experience.
**Acceptance Criteria**
Dashboard content uses an appropriate responsive maximum width.
Summary cards and charts are aligned consistently.
Transaction search, date filters, category filters, and sorting work correctly.
Currency values use Indian number formatting.
Charts display their titles, labels, and legends where appropriate.
No dashboard content is unintentionally clipped or overflowing.
Navigation, buttons, typography, and spacing follow a consistent design system.
Existing transaction functionality remains intact.

items.title: Expense Tracker: Add monthly budgets by category
items.body:
## Context
The initial sample reports actual spending but has no planned-spending comparison. Add a small browser-local budgeting workflow as a follow-up enhancement.

## Scope and acceptance criteria
- Let users create, edit, and remove a USD budget for a category and calendar month.
- Store and calculate budget values as integer cents with validated, versioned persistence.
- Compare each budget with all actual expenses for that category/month, independent of the ledger category filter.
- Show remaining/overspent amounts in text, not color alone; handle empty budgets and zero-spending months explicitly.
- Preserve expense data when saving or deleting budgets, including storage failures.
- Cover month boundaries, exact budget exhaustion, overspending, editing expenses, and reload persistence in checks.

Do not add forecasts, tax calculations, or a backend.
